findings.label: The 4096x4096 2-byte cases are vector-pipeline dominated, and their per-element vector cost is 1.4-1.7x the float32 path
findings.inference: At identical shape and program count, the vector pipeline is the largest single contributor for float16 (18.03 us of 32.45 us AIV active time) and bfloat16 (22.26 us of 36.87 us), while float32 needs only 12.96 us. Normalized per element, the 2-byte paths cost 1.07 ns and 1.33 ns versus 0.77 ns for float32, i.e. 1.4x-1.7x more vector work although they move half the bytes. The kernel body computes tl.log(x)*C on a value that Triton promotes to fp32 and then casts back with y.to(X.dtype.element_ty) (main.py:60-61), so the most plausible explanation is two extra conversion passes over all 16.7M elements; a dtype-dependent log lowering is an alternative. This is an inference, not a measured fact: the instruction listing that would show the conversions failed (simulator deadline). The practical consequence is that timing-3's own vector activity (18.03 us) already exceeds its entire reference latency (15.86 us from the eval comparison), so load/compute/store overlap alone cannot bring that workload to parity - improving overlap has to be combined with, or bounded by, this per-element vector floor.

findings.label: float32 4096x4096 is MTE-busy but the vendor reports both DMA directions below 80% bandwidth utilization when active

evidence.metric: vendor performance summary: MTE2 and MTE3 bandwidth utilization when active
Task Duration(us) / Block Dim (device OpProf pass, timing-3)

findings.inference: The float32 case moves 2x the bytes of the float16 case yet takes only 1.17x as long (39.6 us vs 33.7 us AIV active), and its GPU-side split shifts toward memory: MTE2 11.20 us (0.283) and MTE3 13.17 us (0.333) against vector 12.96 us. The vendor's own summary for the same kernel at Block Dim 512 states that MTE2 and MTE3 bandwidth utilization stay below 80% while they are active, so the memory pipelines are busy but not saturating the interface; adding bandwidth is therefore not the lever. Combined with the coarse 512-program layout (16777216/32768 elements per program, main.py:48-58 and 91-97), the more plausible reading is fine-grained or dependency-limited transfers rather than a bandwidth wall. Prior-round paired context (source c845221e..., a different artifact set that must not be read as this round's measurement) measured 2.69x more MTE2 instructions at 0.37x the bytes per instruction for the identical float16 shape; round 2 changed only the host path (its float16 4096x4096 eval latency is unchanged at 33.88 vs 33.89 us), which is consistent with that device structure still applying but does not prove it. The Memory/L2Cache/PipeUtilization CSVs from this round's op-prof pass exist only inside the vendor tar archive and were not parsed here, so per-instruction payloads are not established for this round.

findings.label: Summed marginal pipeline activity approximately equals kernel duration on all five profiled shapes, consistent with little load/compute/store overlap

evidence.value: 32.679 us summed vs 32.447 us AIV active (33.681 us task)
39.749 us summed vs 39.603 us AIV active (41.141 us task)

evidence.metric: sum(vec+scalar+mte2+mte3) vs aiv_time_us (timing-7 bf16 / timing-6 bf16 1M / timing-9 fp32 65536)

findings.inference: In all three 4096x4096 cases the four marginal pipeline times add up to 0.97-0.97x the AIV active time, whereas at 65536 elements the same sum is only 0.57x of AIV active time. This is suggestive of a serialized load-compute-store sequence at large shapes, but it is explicitly not a time decomposition: marginal activity ratios may overlap and must not be added to reconstruct a timeline. The ratio sum is used only to motivate a falsifiable experiment - if the large kernel were restructured with real prefetch, the summed marginal activity should exceed the measured kernel duration. Establishing the actual order requires the instruction/sync trace, which is unavailable this round.

findings.label: The previously host-bound shapes are now launch-bound with only ~2-5 us of device work behind 12-13 us of eval latency

evidence.metric: Task Duration(us) (steady-state _log10_nomask, Block Num 8, shape 65536 fp32)
Task Duration(us) (steady-state _log10_nomask, Block Num 32, shape 1048576 bf16)

findings.inference: For the 65536-element float32 shape the device task is 2.36 us while eval latency is 12.18 us (speedup 0.954 against a 11.62 us reference), and for the 1M bfloat16 shape the device task is 4.88 us against 13.12 us of eval latency. The two measurements come from independent collections and must not be subtracted to claim an exact host cost, but the device task is clearly a minority of eval latency, so these shapes remain dispatch-bound with a ceiling near the reference's own dispatch cost. This directly supports the round-2 frozen hypothesis (trimming per-call Python work raises the numel<=1M workloads): eval latency on those nine workloads fell 20-31% while the 4096x4096 latencies are unchanged to within 0.04-0.12%, which also confirms the device path was not touched.

performance_interpretation: Round 2 is a host-dispatch win, exactly as planned: geo_mean rose 0.6292 -> 0.8026 (+27.57%), the nine workloads with numel <= 1M improved 20-31% (e.g. timing-6 0.624 -> 0.906, timing-9 0.615 -> 0.954), and the three 4096x4096 latencies moved by at most 0.12%, consistent with the claim that only the host path changed. The remaining deficit is now concentrated in the three large shapes: their ln-speedup losses (0.759 + 0.409 + 0.399) are 59% of the total 2.639 ln deficit, and they are device-bound (profiler device task 33.7/38.4/41.1 us vs eval 33.9/38.1/39.0 us). They are not one bottleneck: float16 and bfloat16 are vector-dominated (18.03/22.26 us of vector time, 1.4-1.7x the float32 per-element cost), while float32 is memory-busy but the vendor reports both DMA directions under 80% bandwidth utilization when active. All three run 512 programs of 32768 elements. The nine small workloads have little headroom left because the reference's own dispatch cost is 10.6-11.9 us against our 12.0-13.5 us.

next_experiment.action_description: For contiguous inputs at the 4096x4096 scale only (add an explicit size threshold above the largest currently-efficient shape, e.g. numel >= 4M), replace the single 32768-element block per program with an explicit per-program loop over UB-resident sub-tiles that prefetches tile i+1 while tile i is computed (2-stage buffering), and size the grid to a small multiple of the physical core count instead of 512. Keep the 32768/_pick_block selection, the zero-numel, masked and strided branches, and the round-2 host fast path byte-for-byte unchanged, and choose the sub-tile per dtype from the actual compile resource report rather than reusing one value.
next_experiment.expected_impact: Kernel duration falls toward the largest single pipeline instead of the sum: timing-3 (float16) from 33.7 us toward its 18.0 us vector floor (target <= 26 us), timing-7 (bfloat16) from 38.0 us toward its 22.3 us floor (target <= 29 us), timing-11 (float32) from 41.1 us toward its 13.2 us memory floor (target <= 30 us). If realized, those three speedups move from 0.468/0.664/0.671 to about 0.6-0.8 and geo_mean moves from 0.8026 to roughly 0.88-0.91 while the nine small workloads are held.
next_experiment.risks_and_rollback: UB overflow is the main compile risk: a 2-stage buffer set must fit 192 KiB, and a tile that compiles for float16 does not imply bfloat16 or float32 (prior buffer probes for this operator failed exactly there at large shapes). Verify the compile report per dtype and reduce the tile or drop to one stage if it overflows. Secondary risks are a regression on the 1M and 65536 shapes if the new path leaks upward, extra scalar/loop overhead, and loss of the in-place store semantics. Rollback: the change is gated behind a size threshold, so restoring the previous single-block branch is a one-line revert; keep the round-2 host path untouched so its +27.6% is never at risk.
success_criteria: All 24 correctness workloads still PASS, including the odd-length 1025 and 7x9 strided cases in all three dtypes.
All 12 timing workloads PASS and the batch's required extra checks (dense/paired semantic gates) still pass on the final source.
Kernel duration (profiler) improves on all three large shapes: timing-3 <= 26 us, timing-7 <= 29 us, timing-11 <= 30 us, measured on the final source.

Overlap falsification check: on the re-collected profile, summed marginal pipeline activity should exceed the measured kernel duration for the large shapes (about 0.97x today). If duration does not improve while that sum stays ~= duration, the serialization hypothesis is rejected and the vector-per-element cost (float16/bfloat16 conversion) becomes the next target.
No regression on the previously host-bound group: the nine numel <= 1M speedups must stay at their round-2 values within noise (>= 0.84).
